title: Watch NE-YO Perform National Anthem at Game 4 of 2026 World Series in Tampa Bay
summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are looking to complete the sweep to capture the franchise's first championship.
contentText:
NE-YO performed the national anthem at game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Tuesday night (Oct. 27) in Tampa Bay, as the Milwaukee Brewers have their brooms out looking to complete the sweep of the Rays.

Holding his hat at his side, NE-YO brought his silky-smooth vocals to “The Star-Spangled Banner,” singing on the baseball field as a graphic of the American flag waved behind him. Watch the full performance here:

NE-YO with a fantastic national anthem performance ahead of #WorldSeries Game 4 🤩 pic.twitter.com/qrE3lHIhZX

— MLB (@MLB) October 27, 2026

The R&B singer followed in the footsteps of Mickey Guyton (game 1), Kylie Cantrall (game 2) and Carly Pearce (game 3) as the national anthem performers in this year’s Fall Classic.

“You go over the words like a madman,” NE-YO said in an interview with MLB Network prior to the performance. “Lord knows that you don’t want to get up there and forget the words. You do a lot of vocal exercises… I try to keep it somewhat traditional.”

If the Rays snatch a victory, game 5 will take place on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at the Trop. But it could be a historic night at Tropicana Field. The champagne bottles are sure to be popping if the Brewers indeed win game 4 to capture the franchise’s first World Series championship.

2026 marks the Brew Crew’s first appearance in the Fall Classic since 1982, when they fell short to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games, which was when the franchise was still in the American League.

This is far from NE-YO’s first time singing the national anthem at a major sporting event. The “So Sick” artist previously performed at the 2016 NBA All-Star Game, Thanksgiving’s Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears game in 2021 and the inaugural NBA In-Season Tournament’s final in 2023 in Las Vegas between the Indiana Pacers and Los Angeles Lakers.

Sporting a cowboy hat, the 47-year-old returned in July with the release of his country-inspired Highway 79 album.
